DfXlmelvIbl.english: What did we do over the last 20 days? We bought all existing filter coffee brands that we could think of, and brewed each coffee using the same normal eversilver filter process. And importantly, we measured every metric that a coffee has—aroma, base level, taste while drinking, taste after drinking, and caffeine level—and created a proper experience-based, taste-based research chart. I am launching that research chart publicly; the link is below, and you can check out the Excel sheet. If you ask why I am exploring all this myself, there is a concept in data science: we process a data set by taking samples, right? The samples in that data set must be collected in a controlled manner—in controlled environments, controlled conditions, and different perspectives—divided into separate groups, placed in separate environments, to test how their body or person's nature changes under those conditions; that is a proper research strategy. In that sense, this research started with the main goal of finding out whether we can deliver a coffee perfectly by following the normal coffee process we use at home (I'll explain that process in the next video). I started it with the belief that this research will definitely bring an important turning point to this business. And I have posted those research findings publicly for you. Now, based on that research, I have made a plan thinking about what standardizations we can bring to our coffees. I'll share that plan in the next video. Until then, have a nice day. Cheers.

DfV_TFvhNQg.english: Neither Soliya aganum... many of you sent me DMs about quitting your jobs, saying 'You are so bold'. Now, quitting a job isn't that hard of a task. You can simply go on the 1st of the month and say, 'Looks like nobody needs me, I'm somewhere far away out of sight, but I'm happy and peaceful,' and just walk away. There is only one difference between a fool and a smart person. If one does something knowing, understanding, and realizing what they are doing, he is smart. If someone just does something haphazardly and gets it done, he is a fool. But if you're really quitting for your development, wouldn't you have done the prior work needed for it beforehand? You all know I'm doing a coffee retail business, right? A few days ago, I put up a stall near the Narasimhar Temple behind Triplicane. As usual, even if I stay quiet my mouth won't be quiet, and even if my mouth is quiet I won't stay idle—I was asking passersby reviews about coffee, asking where they drink coffee, what flavors they like, what aromatic notes they prefer, x and y, collecting all that data and bringing back valuable information to process. I expected all this to work out. But there's a big problem in this. Beyond what people actually need, people only express what they feel; they won't give an honest opinion on how the product actually is. They can't. That's why coffee tasters and tea tasters get paid some of the highest salaries in the world. But when someone has been in business for 80 years, imagine how valuable their experience would be. What I did over the month was compile a list of coffees they daily consume, including Starbucks. Like, each person buys a coffee they like—some like Gotha, some Malgudi, some Kumbakonam degree coffee, and things like that. That's where the main research begins.

Just because someone gets into a fight knowing they'll lose, doesn't mean they are brave. Generally, whether in business or kings in the olden days, when they know someone is stronger than them, they think about how to compromise rather than fighting and destroying themselves. I want to start something new, but what does compromise have to do with it? When we start something new, what goes through our mind? 'Nobody has done this before, we are doing it first, so we will definitely fail.' If you think like that... well, I used to think like that too. If you think that way, you can never accomplish it. People might say 'Just think positive', but the real nuance is: only a person who believes 'I can achieve this' will think about the necessary steps to get there. A person who thinks 'I can't do this, I won't do it, I don't know how' won't even have room to think about the next step. Secondly, the most important thing is our feelings. Think about it: when traveling and stuck in hunger, if we get anything to eat, even near a roadside drain, we buy and eat it immediately, right? At that moment, we don't care about hygiene or luxury. But when our stomach is full, even if our favorite dessert is served, we won't feel like eating. So, just like hunger is a feeling, whatever you want to achieve, don't just treat it as a belief, attach feelings to it, and that will be the best thing. A proper example of this is a breakup. Everyone faces a breakup at some point—between people, friends, or breaking down in what they do. In any aspect, after that particular breaking point, their growth becomes massive, right? Why is that? Because when what they did or believed in broke down, those hurt feelings motivated them to find a way out, driving their growth, right? I personally haven't been to a gym or taken various supplements, but I always tell everyone that taking them and going to the gym is better. De5eijnBp01.english: I started content creation at the beginning of this year. Even my relatives told me, 'No, don't do all this. This won't suit us. Especially when you wear an attire like this and talk about spiritual things, society, or good causes—none of it will reach people. Don't try, fail, and disappoint yourself.' Many of us think that if something good happens to us, we shouldn't keep it to ourselves, right? Started with the small ideology that if we learn a lesson, we shouldn't keep it just to ourselves, I began speaking openly about everything. About 2.5 months ago in July, my follower count plateaued around 3,600. Then my colleagues told me, 'Talk about politics, or talk about movies or some controversial topic—that will easily get reach.' I said no. Because to me, quantity is not a bigger deal than quality. Now if we look at it, there are 7K followers on our channel, and all 7,000 of them are inspired in some way to find a possibility for a small change in their lives. You might have seen my video content; none of it is under a minute. Because I solely believe that giving content in a short span just to grab their attention within a minute won't bring any change in their lives. So I focused on making the content as accurate as possible. They asked me, 'You go to places like the beach, why are you wearing this? Don't do this. People in different spaces will think differently. Going like this among them doesn't look good. You should be how you are expected to be in a given place.' How long can changing yourself for others last? Why do we criticize such people, or why do we think this way—that people should be like this and shouldn't be like that among others? Knowing how to behave in a place is different from how you present yourself. I'm really proud to say firmly that whether it's in a spiritual line, achieving something, or fitness, only those who try to go deep down are my followers. Even if it's slow growth, I didn't want to lose that quality. That's why no matter how many paid promotions come up—be it protein powder, hair oil, or serums—I don't do them unless I ask myself: Is it necessary for the people who like me? Will it be worth it? Whatever I do, I don't want anybody to get influenced just because it's me. As just a small pass-on of what I have learned and experienced, if you openly share what you've done in your life without hesitating, it will be very useful for the next generation. Until then, have a nice day. Cheers!

DeuS3_MTTiA.english: No matter how many workout tips you post, hair growth tips always have a separate fan base. When you workout daily, especially in Chennai water, your scalp gets extremely sticky and severe dandruff appears. Beyond this, if you roam around wearing a helmet to go to office or elsewhere, your head will be almost ruined. Apart from this, there are many other troubles. When we return from going outside, the hair ends get severely dusty. And when we sleep with it touching our neck, we get allergies and itching there. All of this... I have faced all these things myself. Okay, if you ask whether I am going to tell you to use some shampoo for this, absolutely not. I will tell you organic methods using traditional medicine and how to do them. Once a week, what you should do is take 2 teaspoons of fenugreek seeds and about 6 cloves, and next morning grind it in a blender with the same water, and it will form a paste. If you mix that paste with a little curd, it will be a bit liquid, in a nice semi-solid state. If you apply it directly onto your scalp and all the way to the hair tips, the itching and dandruff on your head will completely disappear. If you ask how long to soak it, if you ask me, ideal for 30 minutes. If you soak for an hour, you will easily catch a cold. Okay, after soaking for half an hour after doing all this, it is enough to wash your head well in warm water or even somewhat normal cold water. You can use a gentle shampoo or shikakai powder, or even mix both and use it. Once your head is clean after doing this, the itching on your head will completely go away. Secondly, dandruff won't come back either. You should definitely do this once a week, I do it. And I'll tell you about organic alternatives for hair shining and hair dye in the next video.

This is what I learned from this stall, and I am planning to set up more stalls in the future. Please give your support and suggestions. Until then, have a nice day. Cheers.

DejRbSLxUZa.text: வர்ற வழியில நம்ம நிறைய துணிக்கடை பாத்தோம்ல. அதுல பாறேன், பொதுவா எல்லா ஸ்டால்லயும் சரி எல்லா துணிக்கடையிலயும் சரி வெளில தொங்க விட்டுருப்பான். ஆனா, சில கடையெல்லாம் பாரு, நல்லா கிளாஸ் டோர்லாம் போட்டு என் ப்ராடக்ட்ட வாங்கணும்னா நீ ஏசி ரூம்ல உள்ள வந்துதான் வாங்கணும் அப்படிங்கற மாதிரி எல்லாம் இருக்கும். இப்ப ப்ராப்ளம் பாறேன், இந்த வெளில இருக்கக்கூடிய ப்ராடக்ட்ஸ்லாம் சீக்கிரமாவே சேல் ஆயிடும். உள்ள அந்த மாதிரி ஏசி ரூம்க்குள்ளதான் வச்சுருப்பேன் அப்படிங்கற ப்ராடக்ட்ஸ்லாம் அவ்வளவா சேல் ஆகாது. நல்லா யோசிச்சு பாரு, ஒரு புரூ ஸ்டார்ட் பண்ணது 1 ரூபா சாஷே பாக்கெட்ல. 1 ரூபா சாஷே பாக்கெட்ல எல்லா டீக்கடையிலயும் என்னோடது இருக்கணும், எல்லாரும் எக்ஸ்ப்ளோர் பண்ணி பாக்கணும் அப்படிங்கற ஒரு காரணத்தினால அவன் ஸ்டார்ட் பண்ணான் அவ்வளவு சின்ன ஒரு பாக்கெட்ல. ஆனா, அதுல அவனுக்கு கிடைச்ச ரீச் அப்படிங்கறது ரொம்பவே அதிகம். இப்போ நம்மகிட்ட இருக்கக்கூடிய ப்ராப்ளம் அதான்டா. நம்ம எவ்வளவு பெரிய ஆளா வேணா இருக்கலாம், ஆனா ரெடி டு ஆக்ஸஸா இல்லை அப்படின்னா, we will not be in that field. அதனாலதான் சொல்றது எப்போதுமே, பிராண்டோட ரீச் அப்படிங்கறது ப்ராடக்ட்டோட வெர்சடைலிட்டி பொறுத்துதான். அதனால நான் வந்து இந்த ப்ராடக்ட்ட மக்கள் முன்னாடி வச்சா எப்படி ரியாக்ட் பண்றாங்க அப்படிங்கறத பிராக்டிகல் எக்ஸ்பெரிமெண்ட் பண்ணனும்ன்றனால எங்களோட ஓன் பிசினஸ டைரக்டா மக்கள்கிட்ட கொண்டு போய் சேர்க்கணும்ன்ற ஒரு ஆர்வத்துல I started this stall process. இந்த ப்ராசஸ்ல யார் யார் என்னென்ன தேவைப்படுறது, மக்களுக்கான தேவை என்ன, அத நம்ம எப்படி பூர்த்தி பண்ண முடியும்? அது அனைத்துமே நம்ம இதுல பார்ப்போம். And இதுல என்னென்ன இன்ஃபர்மேஷன் கத்துண்டேன் அப்படிங்கறத வருங்கூடிய வீடியோக்கள்ல கண்டிப்பா சொல்றேன். Have a nice day! Cheers!
DejRbSLxUZa.english: On the way, we saw a lot of clothes shops, right? Look at that, generally in all stalls and clothes shops, they hang items outside. But look at some shops, they put glass doors and make it like, 'If you want to buy my product, you have to come inside an AC room'. Now look at the problem: products kept outside sell quickly. Products that are kept inside AC rooms like that don't sell as much. Think about it: Bru started with a 1 rupee sachet packet. He started in such a small packet so that it would be in every tea shop and everyone could explore it. But the reach he got from that was huge. Now, that's the problem we have. We can be any big player, but if we aren't ready to access, we will not be in that field. That's why it's always said that a brand's reach depends on the product's versatility. So, to practically experiment with how people react when this product is placed in front of them, out of an eagerness to take our own business directly to the people, I started this stall process. In this process, who needs what, what the people's needs are, and how we can fulfill them—we'll see all of that here. And I will definitely share what information I learned from this in upcoming videos. Have a nice day! Cheers!

Dee9CcJTdlM.text: டேய் என்னடா இப்படி வியாபாரம் பண்றீங்க அப்படின்னு நீங்களே மூக்கு மேல விரல வைப்பீங்க. அந்த விஷயத்த இன்னும் நான் உங்ககிட்ட சொல்லல. Actually-அ ஒரு 85 years-ஆ நாங்க வந்து சுந்தரம் காபி அப்படின்னு இருக்கக்கூடிய ஒரு filter coffee powder manufacturer and retailer. என்னதான் business அப்படிங்கறது blood-லயே ஊறும்னு சொன்னாலும் ஒரு proper experience இருக்கணும்ல? அதனால Triplicane வாசல்ல வர Friday, Saturday and Sunday ஒரு coffee powder stall போடலாம் அப்படின்ற மாதிரி ஒரு idea-ல இருக்கேன். Actually we are operating from Chidambaram. Especially எனக்கு Chennai-ல மட்டும் 150 plus customers இருக்காங்க. So அதுல எத்தனை பேர் நம்மள நேரா பாக்க வராங்க, நம்ம பேர் தெரிஞ்சது எத்தனை பேர் அது எல்லாமே நம்ம ஆராய்ஞ்சு பாக்கணும் அப்படின்ற ஒரே காரணத்துனால direct-ஆ field-ல இறங்கி என்னடா இப்படி வியாபாரம் பண்றீங்க அப்படின்ற அளவுக்கு ஒரு normal-ஆன ஒரு table setup-ல ஒரு stall conduct பண்ணலாம் அப்படின்ற ஒரு idea-ல இருக்கேன். இதுல நீங்க join பண்ணிக்கிறது அல்லது product வாங்கணும்னு நினைச்சாலோ இல்ல just like that என்ன வந்து பாக்கணும்னு நினைச்சாலோ, you can definitely come and meet me. Location and timing என்னன்னு கூடிய சீக்கிரம் post பண்றேன். ஆக இந்த நவராத்திரியானது ஒரு நல்ல ஆரம்பமா இருக்கட்டும் அப்படின்றதுக்காக வெறும் வாய் வார்த்தையா இல்லாம direct-ஆ ground-ல இறங்கி என்ன பண்ணலாம் அப்படிங்கறத try பண்ணி experiment பண்ண போறேன். And இந்த process-ல என்னென்ன மாதிரி undergo பண்றேன் and இந்த process-ல இருக்கக்கூடிய சின்ன சின்ன விஷயங்களையும் சேர்த்து நான் உங்களுக்கு share பண்றேன். கூடிய விரைவில் அதுவரைக்கும் follow பண்ணிக்கோங்க. பார்த்தசாரதி அருள் உங்களுக்கும் எனக்கும் எப்போதும் இருக்கட்டும். உங்களுடைய ஆசீர்வாதத்துடன் விடைபெறுகிறேன். நன்றி, வணக்கம். சொல்ல மறந்துட்டேன், stock எல்லாம் limited-தான். டக்குனு வாங்கிக்கோங்க இல்லாட்டி காலியா போயிடும்.
Dee9CcJTdlM.english: Hey, you yourself will put a finger on your nose in surprise thinking, 'Hey, how are you doing business like this!' I haven't told you about that matter yet. Actually, for about 85 years, we are Sundaram Coffee, a filter coffee powder manufacturer and retailer. Even though business runs in our blood, we should have proper experience, right? So, near Triplicane, coming Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, I am planning to set up a coffee powder stall. Actually, we are operating from Chidambaram. Especially, I have 150+ customers just in Chennai. So, to see how many of them come to meet us directly, how many know our name, and to analyze all of that, I decided to get directly onto the field and set up a stall with a normal table setup, to the point where people would ask 'How are you doing business like this!' So, for this Navratri to be a good beginning, instead of just words, I am directly getting onto the ground to try and experiment. And I will share with you what I undergo in this process and the small things in it. Follow along until then, see you soon. May Lord Parthasarathy's blessings be with you and me always. DeU1wPQz2vf.text: முடி வெட்டக் கூடாதுன்னுலாம் ஒன்னும் இல்ல. வெட்ட முடியாத மாதிரி ஒரு சம்பவம். அந்த சம்பவத்துக்கு அப்புறம் இனி முடியே வெட்டக் கூடாதுன்னு ஒரு முடிவு பண்ணேன். அது என்னன்னா போன மாசம் ஒரு random ஞாயிற்றுக்கிழமை முடி வெட்டலாம்னு கடைக்கு போனேன். போன இடத்துல சரியான கூட்டம். சரி நாளைக்கு வெட்டிக்கலாம்னு கிளம்பி வந்துட்டேன். அடுத்த நாள் திங்கட்கிழமை போனேன். போற வழியில பூனை ஒன்னு குறுக்க வந்துருச்சு. பூனை குறுக்க வந்தா கெட்ட சகுனம்னு பெரியவங்க சொல்லுவாங்க. பெரியவங்க சொன்ன எதையுமே நம்ம பெருசா கேட்டதில்ல. சரி இதையாச்சும் கேப்போமேன்னு சொல்லிட்டு மறுநாள் செவ்வாய்க்கிழமை போனேன். போனா கடை மூடி வச்சிருக்கு. வெளியே ஒரு board ஒன்னு வச்சிருந்தாங்க, செவ்வாய்க்கிழமை கடை leave-ன்னு சொல்லிட்டு. சரி பெருசா பொருட்படுத்தல. நாளைக்கு வெட்டிக்கலாம்னு கிளம்பி வந்துட்டேன். இப்ப புதன்கிழமை போறேன். போனா கடை இருந்துச்சு, ஆனா ஆள் இல்ல. யாரு சார், முடி வெட்டுறவர் ஆள் இல்ல. அக்கம்பக்கத்துல போய் விசாரிச்சேன், அந்த கடைக்காரர் எங்கன்னு சொல்லிட்டு. அவங்க சொன்னாங்க, தெரியல அப்படின்னு சொன்னாங்க. ஒரு பேச்சுக்காச்சும் உக்காருங்க, அவரு வெளியே போயிருக்காரு 2 நிமிஷத்துல வந்துருவாருன்னு சொல்லலாம்ல, சொல்லல. சரி ஒருவேளை இதுவும் CM சார் உடைய வேலையா இருக்குமோன்னு நினைச்சுக்கிட்டு அங்கிருந்து கிளம்பி வந்துட்டேன். அடுத்த நாள் வியாழக்கிழமையும் நான் போய் நின்னேன். அன்னைக்கு கடையும் இருந்துச்சு, முடி வெட்டுறவரும் இருந்தாரு. அப்புறம் என்னன்னு கேட்டீங்கன்னா கத்தரிக்கோலை காணோம்னு சொன்னாங்க. நல்லவங்களுக்கு சோதனை வரும்னு சொல்லுவாங்க, ஆனா நல்லவங்களுக்கு மட்டும்தான் சோதனை வரும்னு எனக்கு அன்னைக்குதான் தெரிஞ்சது. இவ்வளவு ஆனதுக்கு அப்புறமும் கூட நான் வெள்ளிக்கிழமை போலாம்னு இருந்தேன், ஆனா போல. என்னடான்னு கேட்டீங்கன்னா எனக்கு உடம்பு சரியில்லை. டாக்டர போய் செக் பண்ணேன். டாக்டர் சொன்னாங்க உங்களுக்கு severe-ஆன cold இருக்கு, நீங்க இதுக்கு அப்புறம் ஒரு வாரத்துக்கு தலைக்கு குளிக்கக் கூடாதுன்னு சொல்லிட்டாங்க. ஒரு முடி வெட்டணும்னு நினைச்சது தப்பா? நல்லதுக்கே காலம் இல்லை. நம்ம முடி வெட்டுறது இயற்கைகே பிடிக்கல. அப்ப இந்த முடியில ஏதோ ஒரு முக்கியமான விஷயம் இருக்குனு நினைச்சுக்கிட்டேன். இப்ப சொல்லுங்க, நான் முடி வெட்டாம இருக்குறதுல என்ன தப்பு? முடி ஏன் வெட்டலன்றதுக்கு ஒரு வாரத்துக்கான காரணத்தை மட்டும்தான் சொல்லிருக்கேன், இன்னும் ஒரு வருஷத்துக்கே என்கிட்ட காரணம் இருக்கு, சொல்றேன் கேக்குறீங்களா? இவன் கொஞ்சம் dangerous-ஆன ஆளு. சீக்கிரம் புடிக்கணும். இல்லைனா இத தொடருவான்னு நினைக்கிறேன்.
DeU1wPQz2vf.english: It's not like I shouldn't cut my hair. An incident happened where I just couldn't cut it. After that incident, I decided not to cut my hair ever again. What happened was, last month on a random Sunday, I went to a barber shop to get a haircut. It was super crowded there. So I thought, okay, I'll get it cut tomorrow, and I left. The next day, Monday, I went. On the way, a cat crossed my path. Elders say it's bad luck if a cat crosses your path. We never really listened to anything elders said. But I thought, okay, let's listen to this at least, and went the next day, Tuesday. When I went, the shop was closed. They had put a board outside saying 'Tuesday shop holiday'. Okay, I didn't care much about it. I thought I'd get it cut tomorrow and left. Now I go on Wednesday. The shop was open, but there was no barber. Who, sir? The barber wasn't there. I asked around nearby where the shop owner was. They said they didn't know. Couldn't they have at least said, 'Sit down, he went out and will be back in 2 minutes'? They didn't. Okay, thinking maybe this is also the CM sir's work, I left from there. The next day, Thursday, I went and stood there. That day the shop was open and the barber was there too. DdyW_0tz8P-.english: Something happened at the start of the year. The people I liked left me. I was working hard preparing for multiple government exams. Mainly, AFCAT was my dream. But that also went away. I have a high interest in technical things. Similarly, I was doing a good job. But unfortunately, that also went away. I've thought, 'Why is this happening only to me?' But I have a small group of friends. Almost similar problems exist in their lives too. Okay, since you do technical stuff really well, let's build a good application, so I waited for a long time, developed it, went through many iterations, and launched that application solo on the Play Store. But even that didn't get much reach. Think about it, I'm not saying this kind of situation happens only to me, it would have happened to everyone. At one point in time, when we look at ourselves in the mirror, we feel like asking, 'Why are you constantly losing?' That was my situation at the start of this year. But I was afraid of just one thing. Even though I was someone who usually feels 'it's fine whatever goes away', when I looked at myself shirtless, I was in a perfect fit like how a highly disciplined person would be. Having lost everything, I decided at least I shouldn't lose this one, and worked really, really hard on it. For me, because I was doing that one thing, losing other things didn't feel like a loss. The thought to change everything would be inside the mind. But to change just one thing, when looking for what that one thing to find was, I mentioned I had a small group of friends, right? Exactly, that was my problem. As for friends, I don't have the mentality to hang out playfully with a large group. Since I have a small group of friends, I realized well that I kept myself inside a small circle. So when it comes to 'you have to come out of that', where will you suddenly go catch a friend? Who will you talk to? None of that is possible, right? So what I did was search if there was anyone like me, analyzing each of their stories, their personal issues—some had family loans, some struggled unable to repay education loans after studying—analyzing everyone's state, I did only one thing. Everyone has a problem. But who voices it out? If we think about where the solution for that comes from, it comes from somewhere. Someone gets motivated by watching a movie. Something learned while talking to someone during travel becomes useful for our life. A Thirukkural read somewhere becomes useful for our life. In such cases, by voicing out what we have experienced, people in similar situations, when experiencing similar suffering, might get some kind of input from that—with that intention, I started this channel and am producing content now. I didn't start this to showcase my talent or anything. I needed input from others to enhance my knowledge and experience. Similarly, with the thought that others might need some drops from me, I started this channel and am posting content like this completely. The video length might be long, I might be spending time on editing myself, even though there are all kinds of time-consuming, effort-consuming, multiple complications in this, I started it for the sole reason that if someone like me is in need, they shouldn't be left alone. And today, I am doing this recording on my birthday afternoon. And thanks for your wishes. Have a nice day. Cheers.

DdMqugsTV3F.english: Recently two of my colleagues were talking. One was bragging to the other, "If you leave something incomplete, it will keep nagging your mind. Dc34PnPTygz.english: I seriously have a question. Do we have control over the duration and the effect of the motivation that we get? If so, when we don't like something, where does the mentality to brush it off instantly come from? I'm telling you very practically, the main thing I get asked in many messages is "what do you do for motivation?" But I really didn't know the answer to it, I truly didn't. I just do it if I want to, but today I discovered that there is an answer to it. To answer all this, we need to introduce a key factor called confidence. So how can we define confidence? According to me, confidence is like an onion. Every peel of it represents each success criteria coming from our achievements that builds confidence, right? Now, where confidence comes from varies from person to person. But a common principle is: when you accomplish something you thought you couldn't or wouldn't do, that's confidence. Beyond how we define this, let me share a few practical things. Someone might be afraid of heights. Someone else of cockroaches, and another person of lizards. Everyone has a fear of something. When they achieve a successful accomplishment that overcomes that fear—outsiders might dismiss a cockroach with a kick, but for someone terrified of it, even getting near it is a big deal—if they easily accomplish something like that, where it crawls near them and they stay calm, how would that feel? That's confidence, right? So how to define confidence? Feeling competent. I thought I couldn't do it, but I did it. I divide this into three types. First is doing it yourself. That's hard for most people because the question arises: who will give you courage? Second is watching others do it. Thinking, "Oh, he did it, it's easy right?" And the third is listening to someone say it's doable, easy, won't impact you negatively, and so on, and thinking, "Okay, we can do this." These three things act as a confidence booster. Looking at it this way, it clashes in some aspects. What is it? You can be confident, but that doesn't mean you are right. If you ask a prisoner, "Isn't what you did wrong?" he might say, "Who says? What I did is right." But in reality, confidence comes when we attach real proof to something; it's not confidence when we just theorize it ourselves. If you think like that, it's superficial with nothing inside. So the pure form of confidence is equal to the courage of doing the stuff really. The level of confidence that comes from doing such a thing is immensely high. So what I'm trying to say is just one thing. If you want your inner core to remain stable when activities threaten your confidence level—shattering each peel representing your goals—you must accomplish the most crucial thing underlying all those peels. And that must be overcoming your biggest fear. Beyond what, why, or how, if you accomplish just that one thing, you can confidently call it confidence rather than ego. And finally, failure builds confidence and fear of failure builds ego. This is what I learned and wanted to share. Like it if you enjoyed it, have a nice day, cheers!

Db0gQ8bTMDl.english: A few days ago, I ordered a phone from Amazon. The phone was good, but the packaging was terrible. I immediately went to the review section and left a 2-star rating, saying 'packaging is average'. Be honest: for all the products we buy on quick-commerce and e-commerce platforms, how many times have we given a rating if the product was good? Now, if a product isn't good, I feel a compulsion to say it. But if it's good, I don't feel that way. Similarly, in our lives, many people will point out our mistakes and keep moving on. Factually speaking, the count of mistakes we make is actually low. I'm telling everyone openly, if you look at the mistakes you make, it's very little. That's because there is no one to point out the good things we do right in front of our eyes, so we ourselves don't realize many of the good things we do. What I do for this is spend just 5 to 10 minutes thinking about and writing down all the good things I did today. Through that itself, our confidence increases, and we can understand what we are doing with visual metrics. 'Okay bro, so you're saying I should be the one to recognize the good things I do, because others won't look at us and say it? Is that all?' If you ask that, don't stop there. Think about it: whether it's people around you or your colleagues, whoever it may be, if you tell them about one or two good things they do and say, 'I'm proud of it, you do good things to this extent, it's great,' what will their reaction be? Think about it, when they hear such a thing, most of them will never recognize that they have that quality. Similarly, some people who realize that you noticed a quality only they knew about themselves will feel proud and then connected with you. Because of this, your altruistic behavior will increase. And finally, if you think about it, the feeling when someone points out a good thing in us that we weren't even aware of is immensely high, yeah? When we give that kind of feeling to others, in some way, or rather in every way, such an encouraging thing will come seeking us. Now, take a person you don't like—someone you feel you shouldn't talk to or go near. I've had a few such people. But what I did was, even if there were just one or two good things about them, I went directly to them and pointed it out. Beyond thinking 'Who is this guy? Why is he saying all this?', what mainly happens in them is—when it used to be 'I don't like him, and he doesn't like me', they think, 'He's saying this... were we actually misunderstanding him all this while?' That kind of mentality gets created. Many times, when we judge that we don't like someone, it's always based only on a few actions they did, rather than us judging their actual character. In such factors, if you point out the good things in them, it will be helpful for them as well as you. If there's one thing important to a person in human society, it's human connection. Recognizing the good things others do is a process to make that connection stronger and wealthier. Just try this out, and tell me in the comments in the future how your results turn out. Have a nice day, see you, bye!

DbOcfU3zsVp.english: This problem started a month ago. As usual, when I came home at night, stretched, and went to bed to sleep, only then did I realize that this was not a normal problem. This is an important awareness video. The thing is, I am a person who workouts well. I know about a proper diet, sleep cycle, meditation, doing this and that, but despite knowing all that, this happened because of a small mistake I made. Normally, I have a daily routine of eating healthy food in the morning, going to the office, coming back, eating, stretching well, and going to bed to sleep. Now, a few days ago, what happened was, as usual, I did my stretches and laid down to sleep, and only then did I realize I had intense body pain. I thought, 'Okay, this must be normal,' because I often get this kind of pain when working out heavily, so I ignored it thinking it's okay. But I usually wake up early in the morning to work out, and during that session, I couldn't even get up. I thought, 'Okay, one day is fine, maybe it's just tiredness,' and let it go. The second day was the same; I tried to stretch at night, it was very hard, I did it anyway, laid down, couldn't sleep, couldn't wake up in the morning, went to office again, and this went on for three days. On the third day evening, as soon as I returned, I fainted and fell. Now, as far as I know, nobody can say I don't workout properly or lack physical activity. Even if I overdo physical activities, I would know. I properly segregate and eat my diet, so I won't have a problem there. Okay, maybe there's a problem with my sleep cycle, or maybe I'm not sleeping properly due to high stress—thinking so, I started waking up at 8:00 instead of 7:00. But even after sleeping for 12 hours, my fatigue didn't go away. Why am I telling you this? Because I forgot one very, very important thing. What is it? I've made videos about working out, how to work out, what to do, how to follow a diet. But an important secret that I haven't mentioned, which I should mention, is that I take an oil bath at least once a week. That month, I didn't take an oil bath because I didn't have time. Having an oil bath gives a tremendous stress-free feeling, which I didn't do. Second thing, in a vegetarian diet, no matter how much macronutrients you consume—like protein, carbs, fats—we forget about essential vitamins and minerals, don't we? So that one thing might not show a big impact initially, but as days go by, it shows. So what I felt was, first, you have a healthy body, but there is some problem with vitamins or minerals in it. Why do I say this? Because usually, I am a strong believer of one thing: mind controls the body, and body controls the mind. When you think too much, going for a walk makes your mind feel clear. Similarly, when you have severe body pain, meditating well feels like relaxation itself. Now, I workout because I am stressed, but because I can't workout, I get stressed. So both of these things left me clueless about what to do. Okay, so this was my state. Based on my guess, I thought my hemoglobin might be low, and I asked ChatGPT about my problems, asking why this is happening. I prepared a list, got a blood test done myself, checked the report, fed it into ChatGPT, and discovered the actual deficiency. Actually, my Vitamin D3 was low. This is usually low for many Indians, but because of this, I had severe body pain. If you ask why I'm telling you all this, many of us say excuses like 'I can't workout, I lack motivation, I'm tired, I get bored.' Check if that's the real reason. Because as a person who works out, even I could figure out whether my physical pain is natural, from working out, or a deficiency. But if you get this right at the beginning of working out, you won't be able to figure it out. So, three things I learned are: every Saturday or every weekend, take an oil bath—do a full body massage and take an oil bath yourself, that's enough (for married people it's not a problem). Even if you just bathe like that, the feeling you get when sleeping then is the real feeling. That feeling won't come even if you sleep on a latex mattress, I'm telling you. Similarly, we must ensure whether correct vitamins and minerals reach our body. So for that, it's not just taking proper healthy food, but whenever a problem arises, instead of thinking you are the sole reason, think 'Maybe there might be a deficiency in it,' and you can also make your diet perfect. Do you know the third important thing? When we are stressed, our mind doesn't even realize we are stressed. So what we should do is, take it as a rule. Whenever extreme stress occurs, keep a fixed template. 'I will do breathing like this, or slowly inhale for 5 seconds and slowly exhale for 5 seconds, I will do this 5 times'—if you fix a schedule like 'I will do this, this way' beforehand, when you get pressurized, you can calm your mind using your body. I don't know who all try this, but try it compulsively. Because of this, I manage anger management very subtly and best. That's what I actually do.

DafbKNTR_lP.text: இப்போ சில பேர்லாம் எடுத்துக்கிட்டீங்கன்னா ப்ராப்பரான டெக்ல ஒர்க் அவுட் பண்ணுவாங்க. ப்ராப்பரா அவங்களோட டயட்டை ஃபாலோ பண்ணுவாங்க. பிடிச்ச விஷயத்தைலாம் விட்டுட்டு எதெல்லாம் தேவையோ அந்த விஷயத்தை மட்டும் கரெக்டா செய்யறது அப்படின்ற மாதிரியான கேரக்டர்லாம் இருப்பாங்க. இத நீங்க டிசிப்ளின் அப்படின்னு டெர்ம் பண்ணி வச்சீங்கன்னா அப்ப டிசிப்ளின்ன்றது என்னது? அந்த நேரத்துக்கு அவங்க பிளான் பண்ணபடி செய்யறது. அவ்வளவுதானா? ஒரு டிசிப்ளின்ட் பெர்சன் வந்து காலம்பற 5 மணிக்கு அலாரம் வச்சு எழுந்துக்குறான். அதே ரிசோர்சஸ், அதே அலாரம், அதே டோன், அதேதான் பக்கத்துல படுத்துட்டு இருக்கிற ஒரு பெர்சனால எழுந்துக்க முடியல அப்படின்னா அதுக்கான காரணம் என்ன? இப்ப ஒரு எக்ஸாம்பிள் சொல்றேனே. நான் பொதுவாவே எப்போதுமே ரிலேஷன்ஷிப் எக்ஸாம்பிள் தான் எடுப்பேன், சௌகரியமா இருக்கும். இப்போ ஒருத்தர் ஒருத்தரை பிரேக்- பிரேக்அப் பண்ணனும்னு நினைக்கிறாங்கன்னு வச்சுக்கோங்களேன். பிரேக்அப் பண்றதுக்கு என்னென்னலாம் காரணங்கள் இருக்கோ அதெல்லாம் தேடிட்டு ஒரு நேரத்துல அது பர்ஸ்ட் அவுட் ஆகி பிரேக்அப்ன்ற விஷயத்தை வெளில சொல்லுவாங்க. அவங்க கலெக்ட் பண்ண டேட்டா வெறும் நேத்தியோடது மட்டும் இருக்காது. அந்த ஹோல் ரிலேஷன்ஷிப்போட மொத்த விதமான க்ரட்ஜையும் சேர்த்துக்கொண்டு வந்திருப்பாங்க. சோ இப்போ நீங்க பாத்தீங்கன்னா ஒரு ஆக்ஷன் நடக்குறது ஒரு விஷயம் நடக்குறதுன்னா அதுக்கு முன்னாடி அவ்வளோ பேக்கிங் அப் இருக்குல்ல. இப்போ அந்த பெர்சனுக்கு ஆப்போசிட்ல இருக்கக்கூடிய ஒரு பெர்சன் மேல இருக்கக்கூடிய டிஸ்ஸாட்டிஸ்ஃபாக்‌ஷனோட பில்டிங் அப் தான் வந்து அந்த பிரேக்அப் அப்படின்ற விஷயமா போய் பிரதிபலிக்குது. இப்ப யோசிச்சு பாத்தீங்கன்னா நீங்க வந்து ஒரு ஆக்ஷன் எடுக்கணும் அப்படின்னா அதுக்கு பின்னாடி இருக்கக்கூடிய பேக்கிங் அப் அவ்வளோ ஸ்ட்ராங்கா இருக்கணும்ல. அந்த பேக்கிங் அப் பேர்தான் ஐடென்டிட்டி அப்படிங்கிறது. Act like what you want to become அப்படின்ற மாதிரி சொல்வாங்க. நிறைய பேர் என்ன பண்ணுவாங்க, நான் ஒர்க்அவுட் பண்றேன் பண்ணல அப்படிங்கிறதெல்லாம் தாண்டி ஆரம்பத்துலயே நான் ஆட்டிடியூட் காட்டுறேன். எனக்கு இந்த விஷயம் பண்ணனும்னு நினைக்குது, இந்த மாதிரி என்ன உயர் தரமா பாக்கனும்னு நினைக்கிறேன் உடனே ஆட்டிடியூட் காமிக்கிறேன் அந்த மாதிரி இத தப்பா கொண்டு போவாங்க.
DafbKNTR_lP.english: Now, if you look at some people, they will work out properly. They will follow their diet properly. They abandon things they like and do only what is necessary—there are characters like that. If you term this as discipline, then what is discipline? Just doing things as planned for that time, is that all? A disciplined person sets an alarm for 5 AM in the morning and wakes up. The same resources, same alarm, same tone, same environment—why is a person sleeping right next to them unable to wake up? What is the reason for that? Let me give an example now. I usually take relationship examples because it's convenient. Now, suppose someone wants to break up with another person. They search for all possible reasons to break up, and at one point, it bursts out and they state the break-up. The data they collected won't just be from yesterday. They will bring together all the grudges from the entire relationship. So now, if you look at it, before an action or something happens, there is so much backing up, right? Now, the building up of dissatisfaction with the person opposite them reflects as a break-up. If you think about it now, if you want to take an action, the backing up behind it needs to be that strong, right? That backing up is called identity. People say 'Act like what you want to become'. Many people think, 'Regardless of whether I work out or not, I will show attitude right from the beginning. I feel like doing this, I want to be seen as high quality, so I will show attitude right away'—they take it the wrong way.

DaczeEJRhpZ.english: In this video, I am going to share a very important lesson I've learned from my essential experiences. What is that lesson? At a point, you will realize limiting yourself is the key to your success. Now, there's a popular saying: a person with no options and a person with 10,000 options is not going to pick any one. Take this example. What I did recently was posting content on Instagram. I can share many things from books. Since I have a keen interest in psychotherapy, I thought I could explore that topic, discuss what applies to our life, and share my personal experiences. So I started one set of posts. But then, since I had complete interest and knowledge, I felt I should do something focused on it. I started posting content on Instagram and YouTube. If you think like this, you have your personal projects, work-related matters, and you are splitting your personal focus into many things. Apart from this, you have devotional pursuits, workout routines, cooking on your own, and so on. Think about it: how diverted it is! None of these are related to one another. However, everything comes to a single point when you try to direct them. What is this direction? Why does a school student go to tuition when everything is taught at school? A tuition teacher's role is only to guide how to study and how much time to spend, not to force them to study, nor can they do that. The same applies to our life. We get diverted in many areas and don't know what to do, when, or how. Even if we set a new goal and have the resources for it, we might not know how to steer things closer to that goal—I certainly didn't. Just trying something new doesn't mean I can show immediate improvement. Definitely not. But by chaining these things together—for example, posting short content on Instagram helps bring the relevant audience. And when it comes to discussing important concepts, doing it on YouTube allows me to direct the interested audience there. That's a lesson I learned. Through this direction, I gained proper knowledge of where to post which content and how much time to spend on it. I gave myself clear direction on when and how to do things. For instance, in your life, if you do something and feel it has no connection to another activity, you must make it reliable and relatable. For example, singing helps me keep a free mind. It has no direct relation to working out. But mentally, singing provides relaxation, while working out provides physical relaxation. If you look at them side-by-side, when you need mental peace, you can sing, and when you need a physical push, you can work out. Since both go hand-in-hand, even if they seem contradictory, knowing when to choose which gives you direction to manage multiple things easily in life. When you can find direction, implementing things takes a lot of effort and time, and the initial returns might be low—that's what I wanted to share in this video. Follow for the next important content. Have a nice day, bye!

DaVpSwrhxFG.english: Here is an important story that happened between me and someone this year. They said, 'You do things consistently. No one else has this consistency. You are a very blessed person, you put in so much effort, I really appreciate you,' and praised me like that. Looking at it one way, it felt true. But are we really that consistent? I have my doubts. I thought: if we are consistent, we should be consistent in everything. But am I consistent in everything? No. So how can you call me a consistent person? I feel like asking this doubt now, though I didn't ask then. Consistency means having the capacity to finish what you start. For example, take a relationship. Suppose I like someone; who determines the connection between us? Just me? Or just that person? There are so many factors between two people that decide and define it. But if I say 'The reason for this connection is solely mine'—meaning I'll text consistently, be present consistently, compromise, and do everything—it just means you're putting too much burden on your head. That doesn't mean you are building a connection that is stronger than anything. As the saying goes, no matter how fast you wave your hands, sound comes only when two hands join. Now, if you call your effort 'consistency' and don't get the expected results, our mind starts thinking worse than ever: 'Man, you did as much as you could, tried everything possible, you were the prime example of consistency, but look, even you couldn't pull it off.' Our mind registers such failed examples. And when do these registered examples resurface? Only when we genuinely need to be consistent with something new. To put it in a simple sentence: If you are in the best, happy situation, enjoy it enough because it won't last forever. If you are in a miserable situation, don't worry, it won't last forever. This is what I learned in my life. Now, if you still consider staying on a wrong path as 'consistency' and board a train heading in the wrong direction, the return cost will be extremely high. Why? Because you lose your effort, time, money, and mental peace. The cost to get back from there will be really high. That's why people say: you can think a hundred times before starting, but don't doubt after starting. But beyond just thinking, self-directing to check if we are going in the right direction is very important. That's why I always take time. Even as someone who works out continuously, I take time to reflect on whether I'm doing it the right way—whether I'm doing it half-heartedly, just passing time, or merely for an Insta post. Now, what is the connection between what I have told with farming as well as AI? Using AI, we automate the central part of growth. But shouldn't we identify the right marketplace ourselves? So we take steps for it. What steps can we take? When launching a product, we first need to research the product's necessity for the customer base. Next is product building, internal content creation, debugging, etc. All those are individual processes, and on monitoring like watering the soil, it will grow inch by inch. So AI automates that specific process, but you are not automating every process in this system. Finally, after it grows, when should we harvest? When should we sell it? We have to figure out if the product's placement is correct or not, right? That is the right time to harvest. That is marketplace placement—delivering the goods into the customer's hands. Bro, even now I say, if you claim 'AI will automate your work', okay, that's a real part. Let me tell you another thing: what every human has is conviction. Conviction means a person looks at something based on their belief.
